title: Brown-Gap Healing and Exact Completeness Thresholds for Leading-Unit Positive Linear Recurrences

definitions.name: x2611_10200_Q
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_10200_Q (g : ℕ) : PowerSeries ℤ :=
  1 - (Finset.Icc 1 g).sum (fun j => PowerSeries.X ^ j)
definitions.notes: Q_g of (1.4), as a formal power series over ℤ. Finset.Icc 1 g contains the exponents 1 through g.

definitions.name: x2611_10200_a
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_10200_a (g : ℕ) (m : ℤ) : ℤ :=
  if m < 0 then 0 else
    PowerSeries.coeff m.toNat (PowerSeries.invOfUnit
      (((1 - PowerSeries.X) ^ 2 : PowerSeries ℤ) * x2611_10200_Q g) 1)
definitions.notes: Coefficient a_m^(g) of (1.4), extended by zero to negative integer indices as in Section 2. PowerSeries.invOfUnit with unit 1 is the formal reciprocal of the displayed denominator, whose constant coefficient is 1.

definitions.name: x2611_10200_M
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_10200_M (g k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ((x2611_10200_a g ((g + k : ℕ) : ℤ) : ℝ) + 1) / (2 : ℝ) ^ g
definitions.notes: The real unrounded threshold of (1.5). Both the integer coefficient and denominator are cast to ℝ before division.

definitions.name: x2611_10200_f
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_10200_f (g k N : ℕ) (m : ℤ) : ℤ :=
  if m < 0 then 0 else
    PowerSeries.coeff m.toNat
      ((1 - PowerSeries.C ((N : ℤ) - 1) * PowerSeries.X ^ k +
          PowerSeries.C ((N : ℤ) - 2) * PowerSeries.X ^ (k + 1)) *
        PowerSeries.invOfUnit
          (((1 - PowerSeries.X) ^ 2 : PowerSeries ℤ) *
            (x2611_10200_Q g - PowerSeries.C (N : ℤ) *
              PowerSeries.X ^ (g + k + 1))) 1)
definitions.notes: The coefficients of F(z) in (2.6), extended by zero at negative integer indices. All subtractions involving N are in ℤ; invOfUnit uses the constant coefficient 1 for g,k ≥ 1.

definitions.name: x2611_10200_standard
definitions.lean:
def x2611_10200_standard (g k N : ℕ) (H : ℕ → ℤ) : Prop :=
  H 1 = 1 ∧
  (∀ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n → n ≤ g + k + 1 →
    H n = 1 + (Finset.Icc 1 (min g (n - 1))).sum (fun j => H (n - j))) ∧
  (∀ n : ℕ, g + k + 2 ≤ n →
    H n = (Finset.Icc 1 g).sum (fun j => H (n - j)) +
      (N : ℤ) * H (n - (g + k + 1)))
definitions.notes: The defining initial conditions (1.2) and recurrence (1.3), with L = g+k+1. H is indexed by ℕ, but only positive indices occur under g,k ≥ 1; H 0 is unconstrained and unused. Using this predicate in hypotheses avoids assuming a closed-form construction of H.

definitions.name: x2611_10200_complete
definitions.notes: Completeness exactly as Appendix A: every positive integer is the sum over a finite set of positive indices. Equal numerical values at different indices remain distinct terms.

definitions.name: x2611_10200_B
definitions.lean:
def x2611_10200_B (H : ℕ → ℤ) (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  1 + (Finset.Icc 1 (n - 1)).sum H - H n
definitions.notes: Brown gap (1.1), for positive index n. All values and subtractions are in ℤ; the empty sum for n=1 is zero.

statements.label: Theorem 1.1 (Exact threshold)
statements.name: x2611_10200_thm1_1
statements.original:
For every $g,k,N\geq 1$ , the sequence (1.2)–(1.3) is complete if and only if

(1.6)

 $1\leq N\leq\lfloor M_{g,k}\rfloor=\left\lfloor\frac{1+[z^{g+k}]((1-z)^{2}Q_{g}(z))^{-1}}{2^{g}}\right\rfloor.$ 

If $M_{g,k}$ is an integer, equality $N=M_{g,k}$ is included.
statements.lean: (g k N : ℕ) (hg : 1 ≤ g) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (H : ℕ → ℤ) (hH : x2611_10200_standard g k N H) : x2611_10200_complete H ↔ 1 ≤ N ∧ (N : ℤ) ≤ Int.floor (x2611_10200_M g k)
statements.notes: The sequence is any H satisfying exactly (1.2)–(1.3). Int.floor is the integer floor of the real M. The endpoint equality is retained by ≤, including when M is integral.

fidelity.twin: (g k N : ℕ) (hg : 1 ≤ g) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (H : ℕ → ℤ) (hH : x2611_10200_standard g k N H) : x2611_10200_complete H ↔ 1 ≤ N ∧ (N : ℤ) ≤ ⌊x2611_10200_M g k⌋

statements.label: Theorem 1.2 (Leading-unit monotonicity)
statements.name: x2611_10200_thm1_2
statements.original: For all $g,k\geq 1$ , one has $M_{g+1,k}>M_{g,k}$ . Consequently, if $[1^{g},0^{k},N]$ is complete, then $[1^{g+1},0^{k},N]$ is complete.
statements.notes: Both the strict increase of the real threshold and the stated implication for completeness are included. The common standing positive-integer hypothesis on N is explicit.

fidelity.equivalence_proof:
theorem x2611_10200_thm1_2_eqv :
    (∀ (g k : ℕ) (hg : 1 ≤ g) (hk : 1 ≤ k),
      x2611_10200_M g k < x2611_10200_M (g + 1) k ∧
      ∀ (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N → ∀ (H H' : ℕ → ℤ),
        x2611_10200_standard g k N H →
        x2611_10200_standard (g + 1) k N H' →
        x2611_10200_complete H → x2611_10200_complete H') ↔
    (∀ (g k : ℕ) (hg : 1 ≤ g) (hk : 1 ≤ k),
      x2611_10200_M (g + 1) k > x2611_10200_M g k ∧
      (∀ (N : ℕ), 1 ≤ N → ∀ (H H' : ℕ → ℤ),
        x2611_10200_standard g k N H →
        x2611_10200_standard (g + 1) k N H' →
        x2611_10200_complete H → x2611_10200_complete H')) := by
  exact Iff.rfl

statements.label: Lemma 2.1 (Initial block)
statements.name: x2611_10200_lem2_1
statements.original:
For $0\leq m<k$ , one has $f_{m}=a_{m}$ . For $0\leq r\leq g$ ,

(2.8)

 $f_{k+r}=a_{k+r}+1-N2^{r}.$ 

Thus $N\leq M_{g,k}$ implies $f_{m}\geq 0$ for $m<L$ . Conversely, completeness implies $N\leq M_{g,k}$ .
statements.notes: Includes the two coefficient identities and both concluding implications. The conclusion for every m<L also includes negative integer indices, at which f was explicitly defined to be zero.

fidelity.equivalence_proof:
theorem x2611_10200_lem2_1_eqv : (∀ (g k N : ℕ) (hg : 1 ≤ g) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hN : 1 ≤ N), (∀ m : ℤ, 0 ≤ m → m < (k : ℤ) → x2611_10200_f g k N m = x2611_10200_a g m) ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ g → x2611_10200_f g k N ((k + r : ℕ) : ℤ) = x2611_10200_a g ((k + r : ℕ) : ℤ) + 1 - (N : ℤ) * 2 ^ r) ∧ ((N : ℝ) ≤ x2611_10200_M g k → ∀ m : ℤ, m < ((g + k + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) → 0 ≤ x2611_10200_f g k N m) ∧ (∀ H : ℕ → ℤ, x2611_10200_standard g k N H → x2611_10200_complete H → (N : ℝ) ≤ x2611_10200_M g k)) ↔ (∀ (g k N : ℕ) (hg : 1 ≤ g) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (H : ℕ → ℤ) (hH : x2611_10200_standard g k N H), (∀ m : ℤ, 0 ≤ m → m < (k : ℤ) → x2611_10200_f g k N m = x2611_10200_a g m) ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ g → x2611_10200_f g k N ((k + r : ℕ) : ℤ) = x2611_10200_a g ((k + r : ℕ) : ℤ) + 1 - (N : ℤ) * (2 : ℤ) ^ r) ∧ (((N : ℝ) ≤ x2611_10200_M g k) → ∀ m : ℤ, m < ((g + k + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) → 0 ≤ x2611_10200_f g k N m) ∧ (x2611_10200_complete H → (N : ℝ) ≤ x2611_10200_M g k)) := by
  have hex (g k N : ℕ) : ∃ H : ℕ → ℤ, x2611_10200_standard g k N H := by
    let F : (n : ℕ) → ((m : ℕ) → m < n → ℤ) → ℤ := fun n ih =>
      if n = 1 then 1 else
      if n ≤ g + k + 1 then
        1 + (Finset.Icc 1 (min g (n - 1))).sum
          (fun j => if h : n - j < n then ih (n - j) h else 0)
      else
        (Finset.Icc 1 g).sum
          (fun j => if h : n - j < n then ih (n - j) h else 0) +
        (N : ℤ) * (if h : n - (g + k + 1) < n then ih (n - (g + k + 1)) h else 0)
    let H : ℕ → ℤ := Nat.strongRec F
    have hrec (n : ℕ) : H n = F n (fun m _ => H m) := Nat.strongRec_eq F n
    refine ⟨H, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
    · simpa only [F, if_pos rfl] using hrec 1
    · intro n hn hnL
      rw [hrec n]
      dsimp only [F]
      rw [if_neg (by omega), if_pos hnL]
      congr 1
      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
      intro j hj
      have hj1 := (Finset.mem_Icc.mp hj).1
      rw [dif_pos (by omega)]
    · intro n hn
      rw [hrec n]
      dsimp only [F]
      rw [if_neg (by omega), if_neg (by omega)]
      congr 1
      · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro j hj
        have hj1 := (Finset.mem_Icc.mp hj).1
        rw [dif_pos (by omega)]
      · rw [dif_pos (by omega)]
  constructor
  · intro h g k N hg hk hN H hH
    obtain ⟨h₁, h₂, h₃, h₄⟩ := h g k N hg hk hN
    exact ⟨h₁, h₂, h₃, h₄ H hH⟩
  · intro h g k N hg hk hN
    obtain ⟨H, hH⟩ := hex g k N
    obtain ⟨h₁, h₂, h₃, _⟩ := h g k N hg hk hN H hH
    refine ⟨h₁, h₂, h₃, ?_⟩
    intro H' hH'
    exact (h g k N hg hk hN H' hH').2.2.2

statements.label: Lemma 3.1
statements.name: x2611_10200_lem3_1
statements.original: Suppose $g\geq 2$ , $k\geq 1$ and $1\leq N\leq M_{g,k}$ . Then $f_{m}\geq 0$ for all $m$ , and $f_{m}>0$ whenever $m\geq L$ .
statements.notes: The hypothesis uses a non-strict threshold. Nonnegativity is stated for every integer index, as negative coefficients were explicitly set to zero; strict positivity starts at L.

statements.label: Lemma 4.1
statements.name: x2611_10200_lem4_1
statements.original: If $g=1$ , $k\geq 1$ and $1\leq N\leq M_{1,k}$ , then $f_{m}\geq 0$ for all $m$ , and $f_{m}>0$ for $m\geq L$ . This includes integer equality $N=M_{1,k}$ .
statements.notes: Substitutes g=1 and L=k+2 throughout. Equality N=M_(1,k) is admitted by the non-strict hypothesis.

fidelity.equivalence_proof:
theorem x2611_10200_lem4_1_eqv :
    (∀ (k N : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
      (hM : (N : ℝ) ≤ x2611_10200_M 1 k),
      (∀ m : ℤ, 0 ≤ x2611_10200_f 1 k N m) ∧
        ∀ m : ℤ, ((k + 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ m → 0 < x2611_10200_f 1 k N m) ↔
    (∀ (g k N : ℕ) (hg : g = 1) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hN : 1 ≤ N)
      (hNM : (N : ℝ) ≤ x2611_10200_M 1 k),
      (∀ m : ℤ, 0 ≤ x2611_10200_f g k N m) ∧
        (∀ m : ℤ, ((g + k + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) ≤ m → 0 < x2611_10200_f g k N m)) := by
  constructor
  · intro h g k N hg hk hN hNM
    subst g
    have hcut : (1 + k + 1 : ℕ) = k + 2 := by omega
    simpa only [hcut] using h k N hk hN hNM
  · intro h k N hk hN hM
    have hcut : (1 + k + 1 : ℕ) = k + 2 := by omega
    simpa only [hcut] using h 1 k N rfl hk hN hM

statements.label: Equations (2.1)–(2.2)
statements.name: x2611_10200_coeff_recurrence_initial
statements.notes: The indices m−1 and m−g−1 use integer subtraction and the paper's zero extension, avoiding truncated natural subtraction.

statements.label: Equation (2.7)
statements.name: x2611_10200_brown_gap_coefficients
statements.notes: Links the recurrence-defined H and its Brown gaps to the generating-function coefficients f, including the exact shift by g+2.

statements.label: Equation (2.9)
statements.name: x2611_10200_gap_recurrence
statements.notes: All coefficient indices and the forcing term c=k+2−N are in ℤ. The range m≥k is exactly the printed one.

statements.label: Equation (4.1) and Section 6, one leading unit
statements.name: x2611_10200_one_unit_formulas
statements.original:
$a_{m}=\binom{m+2}{2},\qquad M_{1,k}=\frac{L(L+1)+2}{4}.$

When $g=1$ , (4.1) gives the known threshold

 $\lfloor M_{1,k}\rfloor=\left\lceil\frac{(k+2)(k+3)}{4}\right\rceil.$
statements.notes: L is expanded as k+2. Binomial coefficients use Nat.choose; floor and ceiling use ℤ-valued Int.floor and Int.ceil on ℝ.

statements.label: Section 6, two leading units and Equation (6.1)
statements.name: x2611_10200_two_unit_formulas
statements.original:
For $g=2$ , define $F_{1}=1$ , $F_{2}=2$ and $F_{m+1}=F_{m}+F_{m-1}$ . Formal-series division yields $a_{m}^{(2)}=F_{m+4}-m-4$ and hence

(6.1)

 $\lfloor M_{2,k}\rfloor=\left\lfloor\frac{F_{k+6}-k-5}{4}\right\rfloor.$
statements.notes: The paper's convention F₁=1,F₂=2 means F_j=Nat.fib(j+1), so the printed F_(m+4) and F_(k+6) are Nat.fib(m+5) and Nat.fib(k+7). Subtraction is in ℤ or ℝ, never truncated in ℕ.

fidelity.equivalence_proof:
theorem x2611_10200_two_unit_formulas_eqv :
    (∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k),
      (∀ m : ℕ, x2611_10200_a 2 (m : ℤ) =
        (Nat.fib (m + 5) : ℤ) - (m : ℤ) - 4) ∧
      Int.floor (x2611_10200_M 2 k) =
        Int.floor (((Nat.fib (k + 7) : ℝ) - (k : ℝ) - 5) / 4)) ↔
    (∀ (F : ℕ → ℤ) (hF₁ : F 1 = 1) (hF₂ : F 2 = 2)
      (hFrec : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → F (n + 2) = F (n + 1) + F n)
      (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k),
      (∀ m : ℕ, x2611_10200_a 2 (m : ℤ) = F (m + 4) - (m : ℤ) - 4) ∧
      ⌊x2611_10200_M 2 k⌋ =
        (⌊((F (k + 6) : ℝ) - (k : ℝ) - 5) / 4⌋ : ℤ)) := by
  constructor
  · intro hA F hF₁ hF₂ hFrec k hk
    -- The recurrence determines every positive index, without using F 0.
    have hF (n : ℕ) : F (n + 1) = (Nat.fib (n + 2) : ℤ) := by
      induction n using Nat.twoStepInduction with
      | zero => simpa using hF₁
      | one => simpa [Nat.fib_add_two] using hF₂
      | more n ih₀ ih₁ =>
        calc
          F (n + 2 + 1) = F (n + 1 + 1) + F (n + 1) := by
            simpa only [Nat.add_assoc] using hFrec (n + 1) (by omega)
          _ = (Nat.fib (n + 1 + 2) : ℤ) + (Nat.fib (n + 2) : ℤ) := by
            rw [ih₁, ih₀]
          _ = (Nat.fib (n + 2 + 2) : ℤ) := by
            rw [Nat.fib_add_two (n := n + 2), Nat.cast_add]
            simp only [Nat.add_assoc, Nat.reduceAdd]
            omega
    obtain ⟨ha, hM⟩ := hA k hk
    constructor
    · intro m
      rw [hF (m + 3)]
      exact ha m
    · rw [hF (k + 5)]
      simpa only [Int.cast_natCast] using hM
  · intro hB k hk
    have hrec : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n →
        (Nat.fib (n + 2 + 1) : ℤ) =
          (Nat.fib (n + 1 + 1) : ℤ) + (Nat.fib (n + 1) : ℤ) := by
      intro n hn
      rw [Nat.fib_add_two (n := n + 1), Nat.cast_add]
      omega
    have h := hB (fun n => (Nat.fib (n + 1) : ℤ))
      (by norm_num) (by norm_num [Nat.fib_add_two]) hrec k hk
    simpa only [Int.cast_natCast] using h

statements.label: Section 6, range 1 ≤ k ≤ g
statements.name: x2611_10200_short_zero_block_formulas
statements.original:
For $1\leq k\leq g$ , iteration of (2.1) from (2.2) gives

 $a_{g+k}^{(g)}=2^{g+k+1}-(k-1)2^{k}-2,\qquad\lfloor M_{g,k}\rfloor=2^{k+1}-\left\lceil\frac{k}{2^{g-k}}\right\rceil,$ 

which agrees with the range already covered in [2, Theorem 1.17]. These are consistency checks on the general formula.
statements.notes: Includes both printed formulas with exactly 1≤k≤g. The exponent g−k is natural subtraction and is exact under k≤g. The ceiling is taken after real division.

statements.label: Example 6.1 (Vanishing critical gap)
statements.name: x2611_10200_example6_1
statements.original:
Take $(g,k,N)=(2,4,20)$ , so $L=7$ and $M_{2,4}=20$ . The sequence begins

 $1,\ 2,\ 4,\ 7,\ 12,\ 20,\ 33,\ 73,\ 146,\ 299,\ 585,\ 1124,\ldots.$ 

At the critical index, $B_{10}=0$ , but the next gaps are $B_{11}=13$ , $B_{12}=59$ , and $B_{13}=198$ . For $N=21$ with the same $g,k$ , the critical gap is $B_{10}=-4$ , so the corresponding sequence is incomplete. Thus equality in the threshold can be admissible even when the first decisive gap vanishes.
statements.notes: The finite prefix is one-indexed and contains exactly the 12 printed terms. Includes the threshold, four Brown gaps for N=20, completeness at equality (stated explicitly in Figure 2 and the paragraph's conclusion), and the negative gap and incompleteness for N=21.
